Definition: of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman):--executioner.
BiblicalUsage: The executioner is the king's headsman. Herod sent an executioner and commanded John's head to be brought, and he went and beheaded him in the prison. One word names the man who did the killing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the executioner shows what a rash oath costs: a king's promise at a banquet bought a prophet's head.
